address: Stadsloket West, Bos en Lommerplein 250, Amsterdam (2003; shops, housing and the stadsdeel office in one pand)
notes: Pand 0363100012118358 (2003, 157 LoD2.2 surfaces, roof max 31.1 m) at Bos en Lommerplein 250; the match step marked it 'no-panorama' because its primary-wall pick had none, but all-walls.ts finds 2021-09-22/23 panoramas for the south, west and a second west wall (the east wall has no candidates). The whole pand is modelled: a dark-brown brick block of shops and housing with the stadsdeel office wing on the west.

South front (surfaces 35/153 and 31/32/45, 2021-09-23 panorama w03-163, sharp): dark brown brick, four storeys of balcony galleries with fine steel bar rails over a shop plinth (cream timber-clad fascias: MANZARAM, FEBO), a taller block at the right with deep loggias, and at the far left edge the red vertical stack of the three St Andrew's crosses on a pylon. West front (surfaces 6/9, w01-285, the A10 side, 65 m): a five-storey red-framed window wall with a rhythm of dark perforated screens in front of the glazing, over a dark mesh plinth.

Signature: the three crosses MODELLED (kit component crosses, red, at the left end of the south front); balcony galleries with bar rails MODELLED (balconies storeys 1 to 4, bars); shop plinth MODELLED (plinth-shopfronts; shop signs MANZARAM / FEBO SKIPPED: temporary tenants); the red-framed west window wall SIMPLIFIED (kit curtain wall with maroon frames, 36 bays; the perforated sun screens SKIPPED: too-small and temporary-looking panels 0.2 m proud); the left-edge crosses stand on a free pylon in the photograph, here on the wall; the stadsloket entrance is not identifiable in the panoramas (no sign legible): SKIPPED not-visible; the east wall (72/142/143, no panorama) carries an INFERRED plain window grid so it is not a blank slab.

The second west wall (surfaces 15/16/23, 2021-09-22 w04-285) is hidden behind a concrete ramp wall in its panorama; the red-framed storeys visible above it are the same facade as surfaces 6/9, so it carries the same curtain-wall group (INFERRED below the visible storeys). Both curtain walls use 20 bays per storey to fit the 12k budget (real pitch is finer).

layeredKit (2026-10-14): a layered curtain wall is one glass skin and cannot carry a blank ground, so the two west curtain-wall groups glazed the ground storey for one install; they now carry ground "mesh-plinth": the glass skin with a closed dark panel over the ground storey, as the photo's dark mesh plinth (SIMPLIFIED: the mesh is a flat dark panel, no perforation).
